title: The Mark Before the Kiln

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The month turns on no spoken word. The hand goes to the mark before the kiln, holds one breath, and touches nothing else that day.
epigraph.attribution: A kiln-house saying in Low Kiln, told at the turning into Frost

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and seventy to two hundred and seventy-two days, six months and ninety to six months and ninety-two days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing — the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the body inventoried as a wound of crust, gap, frozen thread, cold and afterdrop in the order they arrive; the first firing read as an opening nobody praises and nobody mends; the hand's answerings kept as honest objects and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule — with no present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no sixth hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question (the five askings and the one further shaping stand as they stood), no tenth record-first hand, no eighth of the green or the shape, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no name spoken over either sighting, no lesson or sign made of the first firing of Frost, no bond changed hands, no payer named, no private record opened, read or copied, no figure given for the covered grain, no silt-leach or cure named for the cold foot carried below the sill, and no ending.

scenes.title: The First of Frost
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and the first \daymark{270}{...}: Day 270, Frost 1, Firstday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first morning of the new month. Open in the small hours with the hand laid down against the fold on the one hundred and fourteenth answer as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. No recap of Chapter 72; the reader has just read it. Carry the count from 269 to 270 exact, six months and ninety days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy days, its payer unnamed (T088). Body inventory in the old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, past the point where a child would have eaten it, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knows the composed face that is not composure and that a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse; he wants the crust lifted two inches. Both true, the second louder in a body two hundred and seventy days old, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Three counts in three places: the kiln's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor; the river's water over water through the finger's-width door; the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot. Agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands (T061/T082). Frost 1 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 269; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Firstday; the first firing of Frost (Day 271) stands one morning ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it. Smoke's third arithmetic is behind and unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box, the figure read still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047); the dressed grain lies covered and unfigured on the cool stone at the rack end (T077). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells the coals the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger above the charcoal so the tally stays unread (T100), sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, gives every instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot and the water and never to the basket, and keeps the half-pace from every open slate. The widow's mark hangs where it hangs and is not touched at a morning, a hearth, a basket or a bed, because none is an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). The surgeon turns the file out on the towel: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid, nine stoppings with no tenth, the nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth unread beside them; the seventh green stays a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth; the finding that three readings are three and not one account stays on a place of its own with no payer (T061/T082). On the hundred and fifteenth answer the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note, holds for the small intake and comes down on the next low note, borrowing no house count, the three counts kept in three places. No power used, no rank change.

scenes.title: The Grain Under Wool
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 270, no new dated heading: afternoon thinning into the small hours at the Clay Yard's walked-around places, the yard well and bare trough, the drying racks and the space beneath the lowest rack, the pan's gone ring, the terrace and worked strips, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the finger's-width-open back room as a direction and a sound only, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending, the way heat goes out of a pot set off the coals; heat settles behind the pot and into the fold. One crust two inches off, gap unnamed, no third; thread frozen; cold at cheek, temple, wrist; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). Sella carries the basket at the half-pace from every open slate and goes wide around seven things with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line at the Vail corner, the finer grey hairline called the thaw beside it, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the round ring where the shallow clay pan stood with no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word, the bare dark trough beside the yard well with its water called weather, the field's empty place out on the worked strips, and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out. Seven in a row are seven and not an account, because an account wants a payer standing under it and none stands. That hand is carried and not named, not paid, not joined to the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust or the covered grain (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story, his name unspoken two hundred and seventy days: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone years ago to a pot with no crack, the uncalled tile debt circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with; no collector came up the clay road on Frost 1 and none went down it (T009/T013/T092). At the yard well Ilva is glimpsed once drawing with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and grey rack dust in the seam of one thumb; her hand goes toward her sleeve and stays there, the notched birch strip is not taken out, read, asked about or joined to any private keeping, and she answers the woman who asks what the month's firings have taken with the question put and not the one behind it: Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account. The boy files no tenth record-first hand; the ninth stays on its own tray with a finger between it and the eighth (T080 held at nine, not paid). At the kindling Tarn has the small knife at the very lip of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt. He takes the broom only after it is instructed, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late, agreeing with both so thoroughly that no argument can find a foot and keeping the late because it puts off the paying, and tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count. The sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and goes as far as the word that would call the loan and stops there, a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven; the Seed 16 breath is unspent, the chest tight, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is, the stroke over the flagstones without the half-check, the stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot, the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and white in the creases of a fist that had opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and parts them as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, asks neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before any person (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady) and tells a pot You'll do in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either. He knows the full note that pot will give three turns ahead, with air under it and a want in it, and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them. Three or more unnamed men go low into the back room before first grey and get no name from him and no word that the room was cold; the room keeps its finger's width of open and its sound of low voices as a direction only. His bent finger stands in the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, one piece of iron with two bites, mercy and mutilation, joined to no kiln, with no Grathic word for both. The burned-slate word stands at four from Slate Row, a direction over the boards and not a fifth telling; the two shut-room tellings stand at two and do not become three; the three pot sayings stand with the premature Smoke 14 note on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause; the five askings of the row question stand with the one further shaping beside them, no witness under any and no row named; the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn and he's not Vail stays sealed (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101, T061/T082). The house's not-doings are kept as a finding with no payer, held apart from the boy's own kept gaps with a finger between, for a joining would want a payer and none stands. On the hundred and sixteenth answer the hand goes up an inch for the small intake and carries one of the house's rhythms across the little silence after a count in the other room as an object in its own right, crossing no second count and filling nothing. At the going of the light she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the count rests at 270 exact and moves toward Frost 2, a day that has not earned its heading.

scenes.title: The Mark Before the Kiln
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark{271}{...}: Day 271, Frost 2, Secondday, Y.H. 813, the first firing of Frost, from the small hours under the Vail roof to the kiln mouth in the first light and back to the hearth. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 2 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 270; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Secondday; the first firing is the chapter's one real opening and stands behind the household by its close, with the next opening in the first firing of a later month far off. Carry 270 to 271 exact, six months and ninety-one days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-one days, its payer unnamed (T088). THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE: Sella goes to the kiln mouth before the basket and before any instruction, puts her hand to the widow's mark at her throat, holds it one breath, lets go, lifts the clay lid with the back of a hand and tips the carried coal under the back of a broken pot; the fire takes, still answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-one days. Nobody praises the opening and nobody sees what it mended; no slate is entered, no lesson made, no bond changed hands, no payer named and nothing made a sign. This is a real opening under the household's roof — T058/T079 and T088 advanced, not paid — held exactly as on Tallow 1, Ember 1 and Smoke 1. She does not touch the mark again at a shelf, a well, a rack, a road, a basket, a morning, an afternoon or a dusk, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. Do not let the firing pay Tarn's loan or stand up as a tenth stopping: his seventh year stands at its very end and the giving, if it comes, must be earned by a day that has lived to it, and it does not come here. The boy reads the opening as an opening and nothing more; he makes no doctrine of four months' openings and does not lay the three prior openings across this one to make a cause, for a cause wants a payer and none stands (T058/T079, T061/T082). The instruction still goes to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; The house will keep it where another woman would say I; half-pace from every open slate; finger above the charcoal with the tally unread; pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; fold put right without a look at his face; thread left frozen; one crust two inches off with its gap unnamed and no third; cold at cheek, temple and wrist with the wool ridden back; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T060/T086, T100). The dressed grain lies covered and unfigured on the cool stone at the rack end and the arithmetic that will go over it later does not know what it cost (T077). On the hundred and seventeenth answer the hand goes up an inch, holds for the small intake and for the hold of one of the breaths counted in the room that does not touch, and comes down before the letting-go, crossing no silence and borrowing no stroke; the kiln's four-and-a-gap stays under the floor and the river's low-over-lower stays at the door, three counts in three places that do not agree (T061/T082).

scenes.title: What the Opening Leaves
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 271, no new dated heading: the first light going into afternoon and the small hours at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the drying racks and rack end, the walked-around places, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back out of the fold and goes behind the pot. One crust two inches off, gap unnamed, no third; thread frozen; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). The opening is not looked at again as a sign, lesson, mending or payment, and the boy keeps the not-making as a finding with no payer, not laid across the house's not-doings or his own kept gaps, for a joining would want a payer and none stands (T058/T079, T061/T082). The dressed grain is lifted at a corner of the wool and turned once under it for damp with a lighter touch and set back, changed in state and given no figure; the arithmetic that will be read over it does not know what it cost and the space between figure and price stays unsigned (T077). Sella keeps the half-pace, the pot handle two inches out and the charcoal unread behind her finger on top of the shelf's front edge; her lips move along a row standing with two gaps and give neither gap a figure; her eye goes once to the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze and her hand shuts half over nothing; she pushes coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn so the one grey streak at her temple shows pale off the coals (T100). A wrong wind off High Kiln brings the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards, touches the fold and goes out, a direction arrived nowhere, no second edge paid, no fourth likeness made a cause (T064). The seven walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, including the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, carried and not named (T009/T013/T092, T098). At the kindling Tarn's knife lies at the very lip with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it; the ear-sentence comes to the word that would call the loan and stops as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot, the loan uncalled and no collector up or down the clay road (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra's meal-fine dust, his bent finger standing in the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, the burned slate at four, the two shut-room tellings at two, the three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note apart and no fourth likeness made a cause, the five askings with one shaping and no witness and no row named, the promise ungiven and he's not Vail sealed (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101). Below the sill a child's foot that stayed cold after the flood is wrapped in a woman's wool and called the cold by her and weather by the yard; he keeps it as the extremity going before the core with the afterdrop waiting beyond, and names no cause, no silt-leach and no cure (T093/T094). The heard bell stands beside the told bell in the square with its gap where it struck and is not brought under the roof (T078). On the hundred and eighteenth answer the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note, holds through one whole interval of the river's own going and comes down on the next low note, no house count borrowed and the kiln's fifth not supplied. At the going of the light she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft; the count rests at 271 exact and moves toward Frost 3, a day that has not earned its heading.

scenes.title: The Third Morning
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark{272}{...}: Day 272, Frost 3, Thirdday, Y.H. 813, the small hours into the morning under the Vail kiln-house roof and out onto the Clay Yard and the drying racks. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 3 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 271; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Thirdday and none in this chapter; the first firing of Frost is behind the household with no lesson, sign, mending or payer made of it, and the next real opening stands in the first firing of a later month, far off. Carry 271 to 272 exact, six months and ninety-two days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-two days, its payer unnamed (T088). First smells and sounds as before: hot clay under tallow, wet wool, the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; the kiln in fours with its gap, not a bell; the river low over lower. Sella's grammar holds exactly: the instruction goes to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, The house will keep it where another woman would say I, half-pace from every open slate, finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, fold put right without a look at his face, thread left frozen (T100, T058/T079). The dressed grain is turned under the wool on the cool stone at the rack end and given no figure; Smoke's third arithmetic is behind and unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box and the figure read is still not the figure paid (T077, T015/T041/T047). The widow's mark hangs where it hangs, untouched at a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a rack, a basket, a road, an afternoon and a bed, because none of these is an opening and the mark goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn says Yes, house to those who want the thaw early and those who want it late, agrees with both so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. His seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given; the knife is at the very lip of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it, the ear-sentence brought to the word that would call the loan and stopped with no figure and no name, a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is, the loft stone cold and unreconciled, and no collector up or down the clay road (T036/T076, T006). Before first grey three or more unnamed men go low into the finger's-width-open back room; Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger, keeps dusty forearms on one tray and clean ones on another, speaks to the wheel and a pot, puts that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence and gives the end of it to the pot; the promise of the boy's name is neither given nor withdrawn and he's not Vail stays sealed (T035/T031/T062). The grain under wool, the seven walked-around places and the hand that did not come back stay carried and unfigured and unjoined; the row question stays at five askings with one shaping and no witness; the burned slate stays at four and the shut-room tellings at two (T009/T013/T092, T098, T101, T065/T095). One crust two inches off, its gap unnamed and no third; thread frozen; cold at cheek, temple and wrist; afterdrop waiting (T060/T086). On the hundred and nineteenth answer the hand goes up an inch for the small intake, comes down before the letting-go of a count borrowed from the room that does not touch, and leaves the little silence after that count whole and empty on its own place, crossed by no rhythm and filled by no stroke. He makes nothing of the emptiness and will not let it stand up as a gift, a hearing or a sixth of anything (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Count Goes On
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 272, Frost 3, afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed, the boards and the towel. Frost goes out without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming the months is set right or left wrong; no lesson is made of four months' openings and the next opening stands in the first firing of a later month, far off. Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back from the fold; one leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). Garl is kept in objects, a keeping and not a story, his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-two days, the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with; no collector came up the clay road on Frost 1, 2 or 3 and none went down it (T009/T013/T092). The seven walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, including the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, carried and not named (T098). Sella carries him up at the going of the light at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the seven places, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger above the charcoal, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and says nothing at any hour to the basket. The widow's mark hangs where it hangs, touched once before the kiln on Frost 2, held one breath, let go, and touched at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on Frost 1, 2 or 3, because a basket, a shelf and a dusk are not openings (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns the file out on the towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh and none invented to fill the empty place; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause; four low things with water over water a fifth; the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid with Smoke's third arithmetic gone up the road in a locked box and unread under this roof; nine stoppings with no tenth; three held changes on three places, the loft-sill scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, and the held inch on a sixth; nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth on its own tray and her strip unread in her sleeve, and the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth; the dressed grain covered and unfigured on the cool stone at the rack end with the space between its figure and its price unsigned; the pan's gone ring, the shelf's two gaps and the fold's one crust with its unnamed place beside it on trays that do not touch; the row question at five askings with one shaping, no witness under any and no row named; the house's not-doings beside his own kept gaps with a finger between; and the finding that three readings are three and not one account on a place of its own (T061/T082, T080, T100, T101, T060/T086, T015/T041/T047). Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its low note; under the floor the fire keeps four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood; over his head the boards keep four, four and a knot; no fire-sitter stands over the coals to supply a count and no house count is there to borrow. In the room that does not touch a count has ended and a little silence stands after it, whole and empty on a place of its own. On the hundred and twentieth answer the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note, holds for the small intake and past the letting-go of the counted breath in the other room, keeps the small height through the little silence after that count, and comes down on the river's next low note; the held interval and the empty interval are set side by side with a finger between and neither is made to agree with the fifth that is missing under the floor. It is one hundred and twenty, filed on the sixth place beside one hundred and nineteen with no payer named, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air: an honest coordination and not a longer reach, not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a stopping, not a payment, not a held change, not a key, a power or a rule. He makes nothing of it and would not let it stand up as a gift. The hand lies back against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. Two hundred and seventy-two stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and ninety-two days are told by nobody; the carried fire stops at four with its fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-two days and its payer unnamed; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs; the grain lies covered and unfigured with the figure read still not the figure paid; the heard bell stands beside the told. The seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given. Nothing was opened, named, called, paid or ended; only the hand was placed down, forward and unresolved, and the river's low note went quiet after it.
